description: Select a rendering backend among WebGPU, WebGL2, and Canvas 2D, and understand capability detection and fallback.
text:
asciiam separates animation-state calculation from presentation. WebGPU and WebGL2 upload one glyph instance buffer and draw visible glyphs as instanced quads. Canvas 2D uses cached glyph atlases and mode-specific shortcuts where possible.
Renderer selection app.js
const animation = new asciiam('#target', { renderer: 'auto', powerPreference: 'high-performance', quality: 'ultra' }); auto is appropriate for most integrations: it prefers WebGPU, then WebGL2, then Canvas 2D. Use canvas2d for deterministic CPU rendering or environments that limit GPU contexts. Use webgl2 when a production WebGL2 path is required, or webgpu to require the experimental backend while retaining fallback behavior.
WebGPU (experimental opt-in) WebGPU is available as an explicit experimental renderer: renderer: 'webgpu'. It is selected by renderer: 'auto' when capability detection succeeds. Device creation is asynchronous; while it is being prepared, the instance reports the requested WebGPU policy and then emits rendererChange when WebGPU is ready. Failure or device loss falls back to WebGL2 and then Canvas 2D through rendererFallback.
The explicit WebGPU path does not probe navigator.gpu, allocate an adapter, or create WebGPU objects for WebGL2 or Canvas 2D. auto performs one capability probe and uses WebGPU when available, then falls back to WebGL2 or Canvas 2D. While a WebGPU device is pending, frame dispatch returns before animation composition. Atlas views and bind groups are reused after initialization rather than recreated every frame.
The proposed architecture keeps animation and cell generation independent from presentation. A shared renderer contract would receive the resolved logical grid, glyph atlas, cell attributes, resize state, and frame timing, then expose the same lifecycle operations to each backend:
create and resize the presentation resources; upload or consume the current cell data; draw one frame without changing animation state; release resources on destroy(); and report backend status, errors, and recovery events. The contract is an implementation boundary, not a new public API. The WebGL2 and Canvas 2D implementations remain the production fallback source of truth while the WebGPU backend is evaluated.
Capability detection and fallback WebGPU detection is asynchronous and capability-based. The implementation verifies a secure context and navigator.gpu, requests an adapter and device, and treats a missing adapter as unavailable. A truthy navigator.gpu value alone does not establish that a usable device is available. WebGPU is currently not a Baseline feature and is available only in secure contexts in supporting browsers; see the WebGPU API reference.
The requested backend must never prevent an instance from rendering when WebGPU is unavailable. The resolution order is:
flowchart TD A[Construct instance] --> B{Explicit canvas2d?} B -->|yes| C[Canvas 2D] B -->|no| D{WebGPU requested or eligible?} D -->|no| E{WebGL2 available?} D -->|yes| F{Secure context and usable adapter/device?} F -->|yes| G[Experimental WebGPU] F -->|no| E E -->|yes| H[Production WebGL2] E -->|no| C G --> I{Device lost or initialization fails?} I -->|yes| E I -->|no| G auto resolves to WebGPU when available, with WebGL2 and Canvas 2D fallback. Failure must resolve to WebGL2 and then Canvas 2D using the existing fallback events. The implementation must not repeatedly recreate a lost device in a loop; promotion or removal of WebGPU from auto remains subject to the benchmark gates below.
Secure-context and device-loss constraints WebGPU requires HTTPS (with browser-defined localhost development exceptions) and can fail before a device is created. The adapter can be unavailable, the requested limits or features can be unsupported, and a device can be lost after initialization. The prototype must observe GPUDevice.lost, classify the loss reason, release device-owned resources, and fall back to WebGL2 or Canvas 2D. Recreating a WebGPU device is optional recovery work; it must not delay the fallback frame or interrupt destroy().
Resources are device-specific. Any recovery attempt must rebuild buffers, textures, bind groups, pipelines, and glyph-atlas uploads against the new device. Application animation state and logical grid state must remain owned by asciiam and survive backend changes. See the GPUDevice.lost reference for the browser-level loss contract.
Shared renderer contract proposal The prototype should test an internal contract equivalent to the following shape. Names are provisional and must not be treated as supported public API:
src/renderers/contract.js
const renderer = { async init(surface, capabilities) {}, resize(grid, pixelRatio) {}, upload(frame, glyphAtlas) {}, draw(timestamp) {}, getInfo() {}, dispose() {} }; frame should describe cell glyph, color, alpha, and visibility data in a backend-neutral form. Backends may choose different buffer layouts, batching, atlas formats, and synchronization strategies, but they must produce equivalent cell output for the same frame input.
Benchmark gates WebGPU should remain experimental until measurements on representative devices show that it improves the workloads that matter to asciiam without increasing startup or recovery failures. The benchmark plan must compare WebGPU, WebGL2, and Canvas 2D using the same animation state, grid, quality tier, DPR, and media input.
Continued use of WebGPU in renderer: 'auto' should be reviewed against all of the following:
no correctness regressions across supported modes, images, animations, and mesh input; equal or lower median frame time at medium and high cell counts on supported GPU classes; no unacceptable increase in initialization latency or memory use; successful resize, visibility suspension, repeated start/stop, and destruction cycles; deterministic fallback when secure-context, adapter, device, shader, validation, or device-loss conditions occur; and repeated runs across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit coverage where WebGPU is available, plus explicit fallback coverage where it is not. Record median and tail frame time, CPU frame work, drawn-cell count, initialization time, device-loss recovery time, and failure category. Do not promote the backend from a single high-end device result. Until these gates are reviewed, WebGPU remains opt-in prototype work and production behavior remains WebGL2/Canvas 2D.
WebGL2 fallback flow flowchart TD A[Construct instance] --> B{renderer} B -->|canvas2d| C[Canvas 2D] B -->|auto or webgl2| D{WebGL2 context and shaders available?} D -->|yes| E[Instanced WebGL2 renderer] D -->|no| C E --> F{Context lost?} F -->|yes| C F -->|no| E The rendererFallback event reports context-loss fallback. rendererChange reports a requested or resolved backend change.
3D rendering boundary The mesh mode projects bounded geometry into cell-resolution depth and luminance buffers, then uses the existing WebGL2 or Canvas 2D glyph presentation path. It does not turn the WebGL2 backend into a general scene renderer. See 3D meshes and models for geometry contracts, glTF/GLB input, controls, and limits.
Base-format glTF 2.0 and GLB v2 parsing is dependency-free. Custom decoders for compressed GLTF extensions (such as KHR_draco_mesh_compression or EXT_meshopt_compression) can be registered via asciiam.registerGltfDecoder(name, fn).
Headless Server-Side Rendering (SSR) & Terminal Output asciiam.renderToString(options) and asciiam.renderFrame(options) provide pure JavaScript text rasterizers for Node.js, Bun, Deno, Next.js/Nuxt SSR frameworks, or terminal CLI outputs without DOM Canvas or JSDOM requirements.
cli.js
import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; // Render a multi-line ASCII frame with 24-bit ANSI color formatting for terminal CLI const output = asciiam.renderToString({ cols: 80, rows: 24, mode: 'matrix', time: 2.5, ansi: true, color: '#00ff66' }); console.log(output); renderFrame(options) returns a 2D array of cell objects containing { char, r, g, b, a } for custom text formatting or server-side canvas compositing.
Reference Property or method Type Default Effect renderer auto | webgpu | webgl2 | canvas2d auto Selects the presentation backend. auto probes WebGPU first, then falls back to WebGL2, then Canvas 2D. powerPreference high-performance | low-power | default high-performance Passes an adapter preference to WebGPU or WebGL2. setRenderer(value) method — Replaces the presentation canvas while retaining instance state. getRendererInfo() method — Returns requested and resolved renderer information. renderToString(options) static / method — Generates multi-line ASCII text for SSR, Node.js, or terminal output. renderFrame(options) static / method — Generates a 2D cell array of character and RGBA color data. mesh mode built in — Projects points, wireframes, or solid triangles into ASCII cells. setModel(source) async method — Loads core glTF 2.0 or GLB v2; required compression extensions are rejected. See Performance and diagnostics for quality tiers, resolutionScale, the diagnostics overlay, multi-instance behavior, setLayers(), and subpixel font metric calibration.
title: Renderers and performance

description: Install asciiam, create a sized target, select a renderer, and start the animation lifecycle.
text:
asciiam renders an animated glyph grid into a canvas owned by an HTML element or into a canvas supplied by the caller. Prerequisites A browser with requestAnimationFrame and Canvas 2D. WebGL2 when using the default GPU-first renderer; Canvas 2D is used when WebGL2 is unavailable. A target element with non-zero width and height. Install Install the package from npm: terminal npm install @staticcanvas/asciiam To build the repository source locally: terminal git clone https://gitlab.com/staticcanvas/asciiam.git cd asciiam npm ci npm run build The build writes ESM, CommonJS, and UMD files to dist/asciiam. A source checkout can use the generated module without a bundler: index.html
Load a browser bundle index.html

Content remains above the ASCII media surface.

Choose a renderer Value Selection behavior Fallback auto Attempts WebGPU first when supported, then WebGL2. Canvas 2D webgl2 Explicitly requests WebGL2. Canvas 2D webgpu Explicitly requests experimental WebGPU asynchronously. WebGL2, then Canvas 2D canvas2d Uses Canvas 2D. None Inspect the resolved backend after construction: app.js const info = animation.getRendererInfo(); console.log(info.requested, info.backend); animation.setRenderer('canvas2d'); Lifecycle Call start() after construction. Call stop() to retain the instance and its state without scheduling frames. Call destroy() when the target is no longer used. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Constructed Constructed --> Running: start() Running --> Stopped: stop() / off-screen / hidden tab Stopped --> Running: start() / visible Running --> Destroyed: destroy() Stopped --> Destroyed: destroy() Destroyed --> [*] Next steps Review renderers and performance. Build animation sequences. Edit configurations in Usage examples. Preview configurations in the preset gallery. Consult the API reference. Reference API Type Default Purpose new asciiam(target, options) constructor — Creates one renderer instance for the target. renderer option auto Selects automatic, WebGL2, experimental WebGPU, or Canvas 2D rendering. dist/asciiam.mjs ESM artifact — Supports package resolution and direct browser module imports. dist/asciiam.cjs CommonJS artifact — Supports require('@staticcanvas/asciiam'). start() method — Starts or resumes frame scheduling. stop() method — Stops frame scheduling without removing the canvas. destroy() method — Removes observers, listeners, renderer resources, and the owned canvas.
title: Start

description: Quality tiers, logical grid resolution, multi-instance and multi-layer behavior, and the built-in diagnostics overlay.
text:
Quality tiers and resolutionScale bound how much work each frame does. The diagnostics overlay reports that work without adding a persistent timer or observer. State survives grid recalculation for stateful animation modes, and setLayers() composites multiple modes on one surface without per-frame allocation.
Quality tiers Tier Maximum DPR Density Font levels Alpha levels Canvas atlas Static wave cache high 3 0.9 6 64 No No balanced 2 1.0 5 32 No No performance 1.5 1.4 4 16 Yes No ultra 1 2.4 2 8 Yes Yes Higher density values produce fewer cells because they increase cell spacing. targetFPS: null does not impose a library frame cap; the browser display and scheduler remain the physical limit.
Logical grid resolution Browser zoom changes the CSS-pixel size reported by the target, so the automatic column and row count changes with it. resolutionScale provides an explicit adjustment without changing canvas DPR:
app.js
const animation = new asciiam('#target', { resolutionScale: 0.75 }); 1 retains automatic sizing. 0.5 produces the coarsest supported grid and reduces cell work. 2 produces the finest supported grid. Glyph size and cell spacing change together, so the grid remains contiguous. The option applies to procedural animation, images, GIF frames, and 3D meshes. On a fixed-size surface, cell count grows approximately with the square of the scale; test values above 1 on the intended device class.
Diagnostics showStats: true retains the compact FPS, grid, and drawn-cell line. Add extendedStats: true to measure and display:
estimated active display cadence from raw requestAnimationFrame intervals; resolved renderer, quality tier, and effective DPR; mean CPU-side asciiam frame work with a 24-sample text sparkline; drawn-cell occupancy with a 24-sample text sparkline; WebGL adapter text when the browser permits WEBGL_debug_renderer_info; vertex, primitive, topology, raster style, and model state for active 3D input. requestAnimationFrame generally follows display refresh, but browsers do not expose a portable hardware refresh-rate property. The reported Hz value is therefore an estimate and is reset after visibility suspension. WebGL adapter strings can be unavailable under browser privacy controls. The fill chart reports submitted or drawn ASCII-cell occupancy; it is not GPU utilization. CPU utilization and GPU utilization percentages are not reported because the required portable browser APIs do not exist.
Extended diagnostics allocate their fixed history lazily and sample performance.now() only while both statistics flags are active. Output changes at most every 500 ms. They do not install a polling timer, PerformanceObserver, GPU timer query, or dependency. Run npm run benchmark:stats after changing this path.
Browser references: requestAnimationFrame cadence, WEBGL_debug_renderer_info privacy behavior, and the limited-availability WebGL timer-query extension.
Multiple instances All running instances share one requestAnimationFrame scheduler. Each instance retains independent timing, visibility, renderer, and target state. For galleries or grids, construct only visible previews and destroy off-screen instances after a short delay. Browsers limit the number of simultaneous WebGL contexts.
State preservation on grid resizing Dynamic container resizing and option changes (such as density, fontSize, or resolutionScale) trigger a logical grid recalculation. Stateful animation modes (matrix, snow, sparkle, fire, starfield, orbit) preserve active particle and rain-column coordinates during resizes by scaling positions relative to the new grid dimensions. This prevents animation drops from restarting at position zero when responsive viewports change.
Multi-pass layer compositing setLayers() allows stacking and blending multiple animation modes with per-layer opacity and composition blend modes on a single canvas surface with zero per-frame buffer allocation. Per-cell option overrides (color, speed, charSet, etc.) go inside a layer’s options, applied only during that layer’s own draw pass and restored afterward.
Each layer can also carry its own independent image or meshPrimitive/model, decoded and rasterized separately from the instance-wide setImage()/setModel() and from every other layer’s — so, for example, one layer can show one photo while another shows a different 3D primitive, composited together. A layer without its own source falls back to reading the shared instance-wide image/mesh, matching the behavior before these fields existed. Per-layer images are sampled statically (no GIF frame capture); imageOptions/ modelOptions mirror sequence steps’ imageOptions/modelOptions.
app.js
const anim = new asciiam('#hero'); // Blend multiple animation modes, each with its own independent media source anim.setLayers([ { mode: 'current', opacity: 0.5, options: { color: '#005fff' } }, { mode: 'wave', opacity: 0.4, options: { speed: 1.2, color: '#00ffff' } }, { mode: 'sparkle', opacity: 0.3, options: { color: '#ffffff' } }, { mode: 'image', opacity: 0.6, image: '/media/texture.webp', blendMode: 'screen' }, { mode: 'mesh', opacity: 0.5, meshPrimitive: 'torus' } ]); anim.start(); Subpixel font metric calibration Safari and WebKit engines exhibit known subpixel baseline text offsets. calibrateFontMetrics(target, fontFamily, fontSize) and static asciiam.calibrateFontMetrics() measure exact 2D TextMetrics (actualBoundingBoxAscent/Descent) to compute subpixel baseline alignment offsets (baselineOffset), eliminating vertical glyph clipping across cross-browser viewports.
Reference Property or method Type Default Effect quality quality name balanced Applies tier values. resolutionScale number 1 Scales logical grid detail; clamped to 0.5–2. autoQuality boolean false Automatically steps resolutionScale, then quality, down under sustained frame-time pressure and back up under headroom — never past what was requested at construction. maxDPR number tier value Caps backing-store pixel ratio. targetFPS number or null null Adds a per-instance frame cap when numeric. showStats boolean false Enables the compact attached output. extendedStats boolean false Enables opt-in sampling and extended attached output. getStats() method — Returns a structured diagnostics snapshot. setLayers(layers) method — Configures zero-allocation multi-mode composition layers. calibrateFontMetrics(target) static / method — Measures exact subpixel glyph baselines across WebKit and Blink. See Renderers and performance for backend selection, WebGPU/WebGL2/Canvas 2D fallback, and 3D and SSR rendering boundaries.
title: Performance and diagnostics

description: Own targets, renderer instances, application teardown, accessibility, and custom-mode boundaries.
text:
One asciiam instance owns one presentation surface and its lifecycle state. Applications own the target element, configuration, and the point at which the instance is destroyed.
Target ownership Pass a selector, an element, or an existing canvas. A container target receives an owned canvas as its first child; an existing canvas remains application-owned. The target must have a measurable width and height before construction.
app.js
const target = document.querySelector('#hero-media'); const animation = new asciiam(target, { renderer: 'auto' }); animation.start(); setTarget() moves an owned presentation canvas between container elements without creating a second scheduler entry or replacing event subscriptions. Use a new instance when two surfaces must render concurrently.
Pointer movement and pointer/touch presses are observed on the target container. The canvas remains pointer-transparent, so application controls and links keep their normal event targets. Use hoverZone for a moving local field and clickZone for a triggered pulse.
Application teardown Call stop() when an instance may resume. Call destroy() when its view or target is removed. Destruction removes scheduler membership, observers, event listeners, renderer resources, decoded image-frame data, and the canvas when asciiam created it.
view.js
const animation = new asciiam('#preview', asciiam.presets.heroWave); animation.start(); export function disposePreview() { animation.destroy(); } Keep the unsubscribe function returned by on() when a listener has a shorter lifetime than the instance.
Visibility and reduced motion Running instances share one requestAnimationFrame scheduler. Intersection and document-visibility observers prevent off-screen or hidden instances from advancing. When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matches and respectReducedMotion is enabled, the instance renders a static frame instead of scheduling animation.
The canvas is decorative by default and is created with aria-hidden="true" and role="presentation". Put an accessible name or equivalent text on the surrounding content when the ASCII result communicates information rather than decoration.
Custom-mode boundary Use asciiam.registerMode() for a named mode shared by instances. Use customCell with mode: 'custom' for instance-local behavior. A callback runs once per dense grid cell per frame, so avoid allocation, DOM access, network access, and repeated color parsing inside it.
modes.js
asciiam.registerMode('diagonalBands', (cell) => { const phase = (cell.col + cell.row) * 0.25 - cell.time * 2; const intensity = (Math.sin(phase) + 1) / 2; return cell.set('#', intensity, intensity, intensity > 0.8); }); Registered names are process-global. Choose names that will not collide with built-in or third-party modes.
Capability-scoped plugins (planned) An extension API is planned for integrations such as media adapters, audio visualizers, renderer experiments, and custom modes. Plugins should receive an explicit capability object rather than the application, DOM, or global asciiam instance. A capability is granted by the host and can be omitted or revoked:
// Planned shape; not a current API. const plugin = await asciiam.plugins.load(visualizerPlugin, { capabilities: ['registerMode', 'readAudioAnalysis'] }); await plugin.dispose(); The host should define a versioned contract covering plugin identity, compatible asciiam versions, configuration schema, registration, events, and disposal. Each plugin must be able to release listeners, animation work, object URLs, decoded media, audio nodes, and renderer resources through an idempotent lifecycle: install -> activate -> deactivate -> dispose. Failed activation or disposal must not stop unrelated instances.
Capabilities should be narrow and purpose-specific. For example, a visualizer may receive aggregate frequency bins but not microphone MediaStream tracks, network access, arbitrary DOM access, or filesystem access. Plugins are ordinary JavaScript and therefore trusted code unless a future worker or iframe sandbox is explicitly selected; capability names are an API boundary, not a security sandbox by themselves. Hosts should validate manifests, isolate failures, require user consent for media and audio capabilities, and make plugin removal/revocation observable to the application.
Plugins that need a canvas or WebGPU/WebGL resource should use host-provided handles and cleanup callbacks. They should not assume a particular renderer is available: feature detection and the host’s renderer fallback policy remain in control of the application.
Integration flow flowchart TD A[Application creates sized target] --> B[Construct asciiam instance] B --> C[Bind events or load image] C --> D[start] D --> E{View remains mounted?} E -->|yes| F[stop and start as needed] F --> E E -->|no| G[destroy] Reference API Owner Result new asciiam(target, options?) application Creates one instance and resolves a presentation backend. start() instance Starts or resumes scheduler participation. stop() instance Stops scheduling while retaining state and resources. destroy() instance Releases instance-owned resources and listeners. setTarget(target) application Moves the presentation surface to another container. on(event, listener) application Subscribes and returns an unsubscribe function. registerMode(name, callback) process Registers a named dense-cell callback. respectReducedMotion option Defaults to true; renders a static frame for reduced motion.
title: Integration and lifecycle

description: Configure dense fields, spatial effects, reveals, sparse particles, images, and custom cells.
text:
Modes determine how each frame selects glyph, intensity, opacity, weight, and optional color.
Built-in modes Mode Processing model Primary controls none static static rendering for images, 3D meshes, and ASCII grids wave dense field direction, ambient, bandWidth current dense field speed, opacity bounds ripple cached spatial field align, speed vortex cached spatial field align, speed plasma cached spatial field speed, gradient fadeIn, fadeOut timed reveal revealDirection, loop irisIn, irisOut radial transition reveal align, loop dissolveIn, dissolveOut seeded directional dissolve revealDirection, loop assemble seeded fragments gather into the field revealDirection, revealDuration, loop breakApart seeded fragments leave the field revealDirection, revealDuration, loop lumaFold moving folded-luminance ridges speed, opacity bounds riftLace intersecting animated seam lattice speed, character set echoBloom concentric radial echoes align, speed glitch dense displacement glitchIntensity typewriter timed reveal typewriterDuration matrix, snow, sparkle sparse particles matching density option fire, starfield, orbit sparse particles matching density option hoverZone pointer-local dense field interactionRadius, setCursor() clickZone triggered expanding dense field interactionRadius, interactionDuration, triggerInteraction() image sampled image grid image and mask options mesh projected geometry grid mesh source, camera, transform, and raster style chart ASCII data visualization chartData, chartType, chartTitle, setChartData() custom callback customCell Change mode app.js
animation.setMode('vortex'); animation.setOption('align', 'top-left'); animation.setOption('speed', 0.65); Manual setMode() interrupts an active sequence and emits sequenceInterrupt. Sequence step changes use the internal mode transition without treating the change as manual input.
Mode selection changes only the animation algorithm. A loaded image remains the glyph source, including for irisIn, irisOut, dissolveIn, dissolveOut, assemble, breakApart, lumaFold, riftLace, and echoBloom. Preset selection retains the active global mode.
revealDirection supports left-to-right, right-to-left, top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top, diagonal, center, and edges. Changing the direction restarts the local reveal timeline so the result is visible immediately.
Custom mode app.js
asciiam.registerMode('diagonalBands', (api) => { const phase = (api.col + api.row) * 0.25 - api.time * 2; const intensity = (Math.sin(phase) + 1) / 2; return api.set('#', intensity, intensity, intensity > 0.8); }); animation.setMode('diagonalBands'); Pointer interaction modes hoverZone follows pointer movement over the target. setCursor(x, y) supplies the same coordinates programmatically and setCursor(null) clears them. Without an active pointer coordinate, the mode retains only its low-opacity seeded field.
clickZone starts an expanding pulse on pointer or touch press. Call triggerInteraction(x, y) to start it from application coordinates. Calling triggerInteraction() without coordinates uses the current align origin.
app.js
animation.setMode('clickZone'); animation.setOption('interactionRadius', 240); animation.setOption('interactionDuration', 1.4); animation.triggerInteraction(); Alignment support align accepts nine anchors: top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom, and bottom-right.
Mode or feature Alignment effect current Offsets cached field phases. ripple, vortex, plasma, echoBloom Sets the spatial origin. irisIn, irisOut Sets the reveal centre. starfield, orbit Sets the particle projection or orbit origin. Legacy image radial ripple Sets its cached radial origin. clickZone programmatic trigger Supplies the origin when triggerInteraction() receives no coordinates. Alignment does not affect directional, coordinate-global, or pointer-defined modes where a fixed origin has no meaningful role.
Reference API Type Default Effect mode mode name wave Selects the active animation algorithm. speed number 1 Scales the instance timeline. setMode(mode) method — Changes mode and restarts its local timeline. registerMode(name, fn) static method — Registers a named cell callback. customCell(api) function null Supplies cells when mode is custom. interactionRadius CSS pixels 180 Sets hover extent and click-pulse travel distance. interactionDuration seconds 1.1 Sets click-pulse duration. triggerInteraction(x?, y?) method aligned origin Starts a click-zone pulse. Image-backed modes loaded image grid none Applies the selected global mode to sampled glyphs.
title: Animation modes

description: Operational guidance for integration, rendering, performance, animations, character sets, sequences, images, and the web utility.
text: Guides explain how application integration and the web utility map to runtime configuration, and when an option changes renderer state, cached data, image samples, or sequence behavior.
title: Guides

description: Select the default glyph inventory, density ramps, symbolic palettes, or a custom ordered string.
text:
Character sets map a normalized mode intensity or sampled image luminance to a glyph index. The first character represents the lowest value and the last character represents the highest value.
Default character set The default charSet and imageChars value is asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS.asciiExtended. It contains 190 characters in this order:
The 95 printable ASCII code points from U+0020 SPACE through U+007E TILDE. The 95 Latin-1 code points from U+00A1 INVERTED EXCLAMATION MARK through U+00FF LATIN SMALL LETTER Y WITH DIAERESIS. The default favors glyph variety and broad Latin coverage. It is ordered by code point, not measured visual density. Use density, extended, technical, or another intentionally ordered ramp when predictable light-to-dark image conversion is more important than variation.
app.js
const animation = new asciiam('#hero', { charSet: asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS.asciiExtended, imageChars: asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS.density }); charSet controls procedural modes. imageChars controls image luminance mapping and may be configured independently.
Included sets Name Value or composition Intended use density .:-=+*#%@ Compact, predictable luminance ramp. ascii U+0020–U+007E Printable ASCII variety. asciiExtended printable ASCII plus U+00A1–U+00FF Default broad Latin inventory. extended hand-ordered 70-character photographic ramp Image conversion with more density steps. alphanumeric space, digits, upper- and lowercase Latin letters Text-oriented fields without punctuation. uppercase space and A–Z Uppercase terminal fields. lowercase space and a–z Lowercase text fields. symbols space and printable ASCII punctuation Symbol-only fields. boxDrawing lines, corners, joins, shades, and blocks Diagram and terminal-grid textures. arrows cardinal, diagonal, and double arrows Directional fields. math operators and set/calculus symbols Mathematical textures. blocks space and ░▒▓█ Five-level block shading. minimal .oO@ Small portable five-level ramp. technical .·:+=*#%@ Ten-level technical display ramp. geometric space plus circular, square, triangular, and diamond forms Shape transitions and interaction zones. circuit ·-+=oO0#@ Circuit and node-like textures. waves ~≈≋∿ Low-cardinality flowing fields. terminal space, binary digits, brackets, operators, and density marks Terminal and protocol-like textures. binary 01 Binary rain and masks. binaryWide weighted 0 and 1 repetition Binary output with biased selection. braille ordered Braille fill forms Compact dot-density fields. japanese space, binary digits, and selected Katakana Matrix-style fields. punctuation hand-ordered punctuation and letters Photographic ASCII convention. Availability depends on the selected font. Missing glyphs may render as replacement boxes. Choose a font that covers non-ASCII sets and test it on target platforms.
Custom ordered sets Any JavaScript string is accepted. Include a leading space when zero intensity should produce no visible glyph. Use at least two distinct characters so intensity can select more than one result.
app.js
animation.setOption('charSet', ' .·oO0@'); animation.setOption('imageChars', ' .:-=+*#%@'); Repeated characters are allowed and weight selection toward those glyphs. binaryWide, for example, intentionally repeats digits.
Reference API Type Default Effect asciiam.CHARACTER_SETS record of strings included sets Provides named character inventories and ramps. charSet string asciiExtended Maps procedural intensity to glyphs. imageChars string asciiExtended Maps sampled image luminance to glyphs. setOption('charSet', value) method — Rebuilds dependent glyph atlases and static-wave caches. setOption('imageChars', value) method — Resamples loaded image sources and rebuilds dependent atlases.
title: Character sets

description: Construct, edit, and run live JSON configurations with built-in presets, interactive inputs, and instant Web Utility transfer.
text:
The playground and Web utility workflow form a unified composition authoring environment. The playground runs one version-aligned renderer instance and replaces it after valid JSON input. The thirty included examples cover procedural fields, interactions, background images, 3D meshes, sequences, performance tiers, and hybrid compositions combining 3D meshes with sampled images.
Editing model & web utility integration Select an example, edit its option object, and use Run or pause briefly for the debounced preview update. Reset restores the selected example configuration. View in web utility transfers serializable options into the interactive Web Utility configurator via URL encoding, allowing you to fine-tune visual parameters, backdrop, images, and 3D mesh controls visually.
Combining 3D meshes & background images 3D meshes and images can be combined into hybrid compositions. When colorFromImage: true is enabled alongside a loaded background image, 3D mesh geometry (primitives or glTF/GLB models) automatically samples cell colors directly from the underlying background image grid.
The editor accepts JSON because it can be validated without evaluating arbitrary JavaScript. Callbacks such as onReady, sequence callbacks, and customCell are functions and therefore belong in application source rather than the serializable editor.
Package usage app.js
import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const options = { mode: 'wave', color: '#72F1B8' }; const animation = new asciiam('#preview', options); animation.start(); The live editor imports the documentation build’s local ESM file; application code can import the published package directly.
Reference Playground surface Input Behavior Example selector Included example Replaces editor text and renderer state. Configuration editor JSON object Debounces parsing and creates one replacement renderer after valid input. Run Valid JSON object Applies the current configuration immediately. Reset Selected example Restores the authored option object. Copy Current editor text Copies the configuration JSON. View in web utility Valid JSON-representable options Encodes configuration into the utility URL without registry access.
title: JSON builder

description: Run ordered media and mesh animation nodes with controlled timing, retained-frame blends or real per-cell morph transitions, callbacks, and looping.
text:
A sequence controls one renderer. Each node selects a mode, duration, optional delay, image or model-source action, mode-repeat policy, option overrides, and lifecycle callbacks. The web utility displays nodes left to right in playback order; its image selector can retain the current source, clear it, or load one of the included images.
repeat and sequence loop control different boundaries. A step with repeat: true restarts a finite mode such as fadeIn, fadeOut, irisIn, dissolveOut, assemble, or typewriter while that step remains active. It defaults to false, so a finite mode reaches its final frame and holds it until the next step. Sequence loop controls whether playback returns to the first step after the final step.
An incoming step can also declare a blend or morph transition. blend is a retained-frame crossfade: asciiam captures and holds the outgoing presentation before it changes or begins source preparation, then eases it away once the incoming image, media frame set, or mesh is ready and live beneath it. This is a bounded retained-frame blend: it does not restart retained GIF playback, expose decode frames, or run two render engines concurrently.
morph is a real per-cell transition: individual ASCII cells transition character, color, and opacity — or position, in 'flow' style — from the outgoing step’s content to the incoming step’s, staggered across the grid rather than uniformly faded. Pick the style with transition.style:
'dissolve' (default) — each cell crossfades from its old character to its new one, timed by a per-cell wavefront so the change sweeps across the grid instead of happening everywhere at once. 'scramble' — each transitioning cell flickers through a few characters from the active charSet before settling on its target glyph. 'flow' — cells whose old and new character match attempt to slide from their old grid position toward their new one; everything else falls back to 'dissolve'. transition.spread (0.02–0.9, default 0.22) widens or narrows that per-cell wavefront band. morph automatically falls back to blend behavior for scenes it can’t capture cell-by-cell: an active setLayers() composite, a step whose own options resize the grid mid-transition, or while a step’s image/model source is still loading (there is no “after” content to morph toward until that finishes — those steps always retain-and-blend, regardless of the requested type).
The default transition is cut; reduced-motion preference resolves both blend and morph to cuts.
Configure a sequence The following sequence runs ripple for five seconds, fades out, fades in, and repeats.
app.js
animation.setSequence([ { mode: 'ripple', duration: 5 }, { mode: 'fadeOut', duration: 5, repeat: false, transition: { type: 'morph', style: 'dissolve', duration: 0.8, easing: 'easeInOut' } }, { mode: 'fadeIn', duration: 1, transition: { type: 'morph', style: 'scramble', duration: 0.8, easing: 'easeInOut' } } ], { loop: true, autoplay: true, onStepStart(detail) { console.log(detail.index, detail.step.mode); } }); Move between images Set image to a URL to decode and sample a new source before that node starts. Omit the field to retain the current source, or use null to clear image data and return to a procedural grid. A node’s delay elapses first; its duration does not begin until the new image is ready. This prevents decode time from shortening the visible node.
animation.setSequence([ { mode: 'fadeIn', image: '/media/product-front.webp', duration: 3 }, { mode: 'lumaFold', image: '/media/product-detail.webp', imageOptions: { animated: false }, duration: 4, // A step that loads a new image source always retains-and-blends while it decodes, // regardless of the requested type — there is no "after" content to morph toward yet. transition: { type: 'blend', duration: 0.6, easing: 'easeInOut' } }, { mode: 'wave', image: null, duration: 2 } ], { autoplay: true, loop: true }); animation.on('sequenceStepError', ({ index, error }) => { console.error(`Image for node ${index + 1} could not be loaded`, error); }); An image failure pauses the sequence, calls the node’s optional onError, and emits sequenceStepError. Correct the source or seek to another node before resuming.
Move between 3D models Set model to a URL or other setModel() source to load glTF/GLB geometry before a mesh node starts. Omit it to retain the current mesh, or set it to null to clear geometry. modelOptions accepts the same bounded loader options as setModel(). meshEnabled defaults to false; set it (globally at construction, or per step via options) for a mesh step’s geometry to actually render.
animation.setSequence([ { mode: 'mesh', model: '/models/part-a.glb', options: { meshEnabled: true }, duration: 4 }, { mode: 'mesh', model: '/models/part-b.glb', options: { meshStyle: 'wireframe', meshAutoRotate: true }, duration: 4, // Same as image loads: a step that loads a new model source always retains-and-blends. transition: { type: 'blend', duration: 0.7, easing: 'easeInOut' } } ], { autoplay: true }); Model load or validation failure follows the same onError and sequenceStepError path as image failure.
delay staggers the start of a step. During the delay, the prior frame state continues. duration begins after the delay completes.
Sequence state stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Configured: setSequence() Configured --> Waiting: playSequence() + delay Configured --> Playing: playSequence() Waiting --> Loading: node declares a new image or model Loading --> Playing: source decoded and sampled Loading --> Paused: source error Waiting --> Playing: delay elapsed, image retained or cleared Playing --> Waiting: next step has delay Playing --> Playing: next step Playing --> Paused: pauseSequence() Paused --> Playing: playSequence() Playing --> Complete: last step and loop=false Playing --> Configured: stopSequence() Playing --> Interrupted: manual setMode() Callbacks and events Step callbacks receive (detail, animation). The same lifecycle is available through on() event subscriptions when configuration should remain serializable.
Reference API Input Result setSequence(steps, options) step array, sequence options Configures a sequence and returns the instance. playSequence(index?) optional start index Starts or resumes playback. pauseSequence(reason?) optional reason Pauses at the current step. stopSequence() none Stops playback and resets sequence position. clearSequence() none Removes sequence configuration. seekSequence(index) numeric index Interrupts the current step and selects another. nextSequenceStep() none Advances one step using loop policy. getSequenceState() none Returns configured, running, completed, index, length, loop, elapsed, waiting, loading, and morph state. step.image string, null, or omitted Loads a source, clears the current source, or retains it. step.imageOptions object Passes image decode hints such as animated to setImage(). step.model source, null, or omitted Loads a glTF/GLB source, clears geometry, or retains it. step.modelOptions object Passes bounded loader options to setModel(). step.onError callback Runs when the node’s image or model cannot be decoded. step.repeat boolean, default false Repeats a finite mode timeline while the step remains active. step.transition { type, duration, easing } Selects an incoming cut or snapshot morph; duration uses seconds. options.loop boolean, default true Restarts the sequence after its final step. sequenceMorphStart event Emitted after incoming state is ready and the retained outgoing frame begins easing away. sequenceMorphComplete event Emitted after the outgoing snapshot reaches zero opacity. sequenceStepError event Emitted when a node image or model fails; playback pauses.

The package exports the asciiam class as its default export and includes TypeScript declarations in src/asciiam.d.ts.

Mutating methods apply to the live instance; sequence methods return the instance for chaining.
Constructor app.js
import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const animation = new asciiam('#target', { mode: 'wave', renderer: 'auto', quality: 'balanced' }); new asciiam(target, options?) Parameter Type Required Description target CSS selector, HTMLElement, or HTMLCanvasElement Yes Container that receives an owned canvas, or a caller-owned canvas. options asciiamOptions No Initial renderer, mode, presentation, image, and lifecycle configuration. The constructor throws when the target cannot be found or when renderer has an unsupported value. If neither Canvas 2D nor WebGL2 can initialize, the instance becomes a no-op and logs a warning.
Target ownership Passing a container lets asciiam create and own its presentation canvas. Passing an HTMLCanvasElement uses the caller-supplied canvas. In both cases, call destroy() before permanently removing the instance so renderer resources and observers are released.

Option Type Default Description cols number 80 Grid column width. rows number 24 Grid row height. mode string 'matrix' Animation mode name ('matrix', 'plasma', 'wave', 'fire', 'snow', etc.). time number 0 Time offset in seconds for deterministic frame rendering. charSet string 'ascii-extended' Character set preset or explicit glyph string. invert boolean false Inverts glyph intensity mapping. ansi boolean false Injects 24-bit ANSI color escape codes (\x1b[38;2;R;G;Bm) into string output. color string '#00ff66' Base hex foreground color used for ANSI escape sequences. getStats() Extended timing fields remain null until showStats and extendedStats are active and the first reporting interval completes. Field Type Description fps number Rendered instance frames per reporting interval. estimatedRefreshRate number or null Active animation-frame cadence estimate in Hz. frameWorkMs number or null Mean CPU-side asciiam frame work in milliseconds. cells / drawn number Total grid cells and cells submitted or drawn in the latest frame. occupancy number drawn / cells; not CPU or GPU utilization. renderer object Backend policy, resolved context flags, and optional adapter strings. quality / dpr / targetFPS mixed Current quality and presentation limits. reducedMotion boolean Resolved reduced-motion state. mesh mesh summary Retained topology and raster controls. modelLoaded boolean Whether active geometry originated from model input. Sequence objects Sequence step Property Type Required Description id string No Stable application identifier. label string No Application-facing label. mode mode string Yes Mode activated for the step. duration seconds No Active step duration. delay seconds No Wait before step activation. repeat boolean No Repeats a finite mode timeline within the step; defaults to false. image string, null, or omitted No Decodes a new source before timing starts, clears the source, or retains it when omitted. imageOptions image option record No Passes decode hints such as animated to setImage(). model glTF/GLB source, null, or omitted No Decodes new geometry before timing starts, clears geometry, or retains it when omitted. modelOptions model load option record No Passes loader limits, scene selection, and progress handling to setModel(). options option record No Step-local option overrides. transition transition object No Incoming cut, retained-frame blend, or real per-cell morph transition. See Animation sequences for morph’s style/spread fields. onStart callback No Runs when the step starts. onComplete callback No Runs on normal completion. onInterrupt callback No Runs when interrupted. onError callback No Runs when a step image or model fails to load; playback pauses. Sequence options Property Type Default Description loop boolean true behavior Restarts after the final step. autoplay boolean false Starts after configuration. onStepStart callback null Runs for each start. onStepComplete callback null Runs for each normal completion. onStepInterrupt callback null Runs for each interruption. onComplete callback null Runs when a non-looping sequence completes. Sequence methods Method Return Description setSequence(steps, options?) instance Configures ordered steps. playSequence(startIndex?) instance Starts or resumes playback. pauseSequence(reason?) instance Pauses playback. stopSequence() instance Stops and resets playback. clearSequence() instance Removes sequence configuration. seekSequence(index) instance Interrupts and selects a normalized index. nextSequenceStep() instance Advances according to loop policy. getSequenceState() state object Returns current playback state. Sequence state Field Type Description configured boolean Whether steps exist. running boolean Whether sequence time advances. completed boolean Whether a non-looping sequence reached its final boundary. index number Active step index or -1. length number Step count. loop boolean Active loop policy. elapsed number Seconds elapsed in the current phase. waiting boolean Whether the active step delay is pending. loading boolean Whether the active step is waiting for an image decode. Duration remains at zero. morphing boolean Whether a blend or morph transition is currently in progress. morphProgress number Normalized transition progress from 0 through 1. Events Subscribe with on(event, listener). The method returns an unsubscribe function. Remove a known listener with off(event, listener).
app.js
const unsubscribe = animation.on('rendererFallback', (detail, instance) => { console.log(detail.reason, detail.backend, instance); }); unsubscribe(); Keep the returned unsubscribe function when a listener belongs to a component lifecycle. off(event, listener) is useful when the same stable listener reference is already available.
Event Trigger ready Construction and initial sizing complete. resize Target grid dimensions change. frame A frame is rendered. rendererChange Requested or resolved renderer changes. rendererFallback WebGL context loss switches presentation to Canvas 2D. autoQualityChange autoQuality steps resolutionScale or quality; detail includes reason ('pressure' or 'recovery'), the new quality/resolutionScale, and the measured frameWorkMs. imageFramesReady Exact GIF capture completes; detail includes frameCount and total duration in seconds. meshReady, meshClear Retained geometry is installed or released. modelLoadStart, modelProgress Model loading starts or reports transferred bytes. modelReady, modelError, modelClear Model normalization succeeds, fails, or is cleared. sequenceStart, sequenceResume Sequence playback starts or resumes. sequencePause, sequenceStop Playback pauses or stops. sequenceLoop, sequenceComplete Sequence loops or finishes. sequenceInterrupt Manual mode selection interrupts playback. sequenceStepStart A delayed or immediate step starts. sequenceStepComplete A step reaches its duration. sequenceStepInterrupt Seek, stop, reconfiguration, or manual input interrupts a step. sequenceStepError A step image fails to decode; detail contains error and playback pauses. sequenceMorphStart, sequenceMorphComplete A step’s blend or morph transition begins or finishes. Callback types Callback Signature Description Ready (animation) => void Constructor readiness callback. Image error (error) => void Image decode or load failure callback. Event listener (detail, animation) => void General event subscription. Sequence callback (detail, animation) => void Step or sequence lifecycle callback. Custom cell (api) => cell | null Returns a glyph cell for one grid coordinate. TypeScript surface The bundled declarations export asciiamMode, asciiamEvent, asciiamOptions, sequence step/options/state types, event detail, and the default asciiam class. Import types alongside the runtime without a separate package.
import asciiam, { type asciiamOptions, type asciiamSequenceStep } from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const options: asciiamOptions = { renderer: 'auto', quality: 'balanced' }; const steps: asciiamSequenceStep[] = [ { mode: 'ripple', duration: 5 }, { mode: 'fadeOut', duration: 1.2 } ]; const animation = new asciiam('#target', options).setSequence(steps, { loop: true, autoplay: true });
title: API reference

description: Sample local or remote images into ASCII and restrict animation to an inclusive RGB range.
text: Image loading establishes a sampled glyph source. Static images are resampled after grid or image-option changes. Animated GIFs capture each composited frame as an ASCII grid when WebCodecs ImageDecoder is available. Brightness selects glyph density. Optional sampled RGB values color each glyph. The global mode then animates that source, so the same mode inventory applies to procedural and image-backed output. Planned media asset lifecycle Media support is planned as an explicit application-owned lifecycle: Acquire a URL, File, or user-selected Blob only after the application has established the required permission and consent state. Validate the media type and size before decoding, then create a short-lived object URL or stream for the loader. Decode and sample frames into the active ASCII grid. Retain compact sampled data where possible instead of full-resolution frame buffers. Revoke object URLs and release decoders, tracks, audio nodes, and frame data when the asset is replaced or the asciiam instance is destroyed. Applications should treat remote media as untrusted input: use HTTPS, configure appropriate CORS headers, and avoid copying user media to a server unless that is an explicit product decision. A future media adapter may expose progress, cancellation, memory limits, and disposal hooks without changing the renderer API. Local media and audio visualization (planned) Local and user-selected media should remain local by default. File inputs and drag- and-drop can provide File objects to an application-level adapter, while camera and microphone sources require an explicit getUserMedia() permission request. The adapter should make ownership clear: the application owns the MediaStream, and stopping its tracks is part of teardown. An audio visualizer can feed an asciiam mode through the Web Audio API without coupling audio processing to the renderer. The planned data flow is: audio element or MediaStream -> AudioContext -> AnalyserNode -> Uint8Array frequency/time-domain samples -> visualizer adapter or plugin -> mode parameters / sampled cells -> asciiam renderer AnalyserNode.getByteFrequencyData() is suitable for spectrum bars and getByteTimeDomainData() for waveform-driven motion. The adapter should reuse typed-array buffers, throttle analysis to the render cadence, suspend the audio context when hidden, and disconnect nodes during disposal. It should not expose raw microphone samples to a plugin unless the user has explicitly granted that capability. Visualizers must provide a non-audio alternative, respect prefers-reduced-motion, and avoid implying that microphone access is available until permission succeeds. The permission prompt should be initiated by a clear user action and its denied, revoked, and unavailable states should be represented as ordinary fallback UI. Load an image app.js await animation.setImage('/images/subject.webp'); animation.setMode('ripple'); animation.setOption('colorFromImage', true); Uploaded files can be passed through an object URL. Revoke the URL after setImage() resolves. URL paths ending in .gif and GIF data URLs are detected automatically. A blob URL does not contain the source filename or media type in its URL string, so pass { animated: true } when loading an uploaded GIF. setImage() waits while each decoded frame is converted to the current ASCII grid, preserves individual frame delays, and emits imageFramesReady with frameCount and total duration. Each decoded bitmap is closed after conversion; playback retains ASCII cell data rather than full-resolution frames. Frame conversion is preparation, not playback. asciiam keeps the current grid visible through the decode pass and publishes the completed frame set atomically at frame zero. Decoded frames therefore cannot appear before scheduled playback begins. If ImageDecoder or fetch access is unavailable, asciiam falls back to sampling the browser-animated . imageFrameRate limits only that compatibility path; it does not alter exact GIF frame delays or cap renderer FPS. Changing image sampling options or target dimensions re-captures the ASCII frames after a short debounce. app.js await animation.setImage(objectUrl, { animated: file.type === 'image/gif' }); animation.setOption('imageFrameRate', 12); Animate a colour range app.js animation.setOption('imageAnimationRange', { min: '#7a0000', max: '#ff8a70' }); animation.setMode('ripple'); Procedural, reveal, interaction, sparse-particle, and custom modes can operate while an image source is loaded. Dense modes animate sampled glyph cells directly. Sparse modes such as matrix, snow, fire, starfield, and orbit retain their particle geometry and are clipped to sampled image cells. mesh renders its 3D geometry source; when colorFromImage is enabled alongside a loaded image, 3D mesh characters sample cell colors directly from the background image grid, allowing textured 3D ASCII compositions. Transparent SVG silhouettes often use black fills. Normal luminance mapping sends black to the first density glyph, which is commonly a space. The default imageLuminance: 'auto' detects dark opaque artwork surrounded by transparency and inverts its density mapping. Set normal or invert when explicit control is required. This affects glyph density only; it does not rotate or transform the source SVG. Image fitting compares the source aspect ratio with the rendered glyph area, including the measured glyph width and line height. imageScale and imageFov change the centered source window. imageScaleX and imageScaleY then change the centered sampled output width and height. This distinction preserves the source ratio by default while allowing intentional horizontal or vertical distortion. imageRotation rotates the fitted source clockwise in degrees. imageFlipX and imageFlipY mirror it horizontally or vertically. These transforms run only while sampling or recapturing image grids; they do not add work to frames between sampling operations. ASCII text sources JavaScript FIGlet implementations can convert text into multiline ASCII banners before rendering. The figlet package provides browser and ESM builds and implements the FIGfont format. Keep it as an application-level optional adapter so asciiam retains zero runtime dependencies: generate the banner, rasterize it to a canvas or SVG data URL, then pass that result to setImage() and select any global mode. The engine creates a byte mask during image sampling. Per-frame image animation checks the mask rather than repeating RGB range comparisons. Cells outside the range remain static. Mask modes Value Behavior waveSweep Moves a horizontal intensity band through selected cells. radialRipple Propagates from the configured spatial origin. scanlinePass Moves a narrow scanline over selected cells. thermalNoise Applies time-varying seeded noise. halftonePulse Pulses a spatial halftone pattern. fullStatic Displays sampled glyphs without mask animation. Reference Property or method Type Default Effect setImage(source, options?) URL string and optional { animated } — Decodes an image and captures GIF frames when ImageDecoder and fetch access are available. fit cover | contain cover Crops or letterboxes the source. imageScale number 1 Applies centered source zoom. imageScaleX number 1 Scales sampled output width around the centre. imageScaleY number 1 Scales sampled output height around the centre. imageFov number 1 Controls the sampled field of view. imageRotation degrees 0 Rotates the fitted source clockwise during sampling. imageFlipX / imageFlipY boolean false Mirrors the sampled source by axis. imageLuminance auto | normal | invert auto Controls silhouette-aware brightness mapping. imageChars string active character set Maps brightness to glyphs. colorFromImage boolean false Uses sampled RGB values. animateImageMask boolean true Enables legacy mode: 'image' mask animation; global modes animate image sources independently. imageAnimationRange { min, max } or null null Restricts animation to an inclusive RGB box. animateImageFrames boolean true Plays captured or fallback-sampled GIF frames. imageFrameRate number 12 Caps fallback GIF sampling from 1 through 60 fps.

description: Render typed-array meshes, procedural primitives, and dependency-free glTF 2.0 or GLB v2 files as ASCII.
text:
The mesh mode projects geometry into a cell-resolution depth and luminance buffer. The normal asciiam glyph pipeline then presents those cells through WebGL2 or Canvas 2D. It is a bounded ASCII source, not a general scene engine: materials, textures, animation clips, skins, cameras, and lights from glTF are not rendered.
Procedural geometry const animation = new asciiam('#target', { mode: 'mesh', meshEnabled: true, // meshEnabled/imageEnabled default to false meshPrimitive: 'torus', meshStyle: 'wireframe', meshAutoRotate: true }); animation.start(); cube, plane, icosphere, and torus are generated at construction time without bundled model assets. For explicit control, call asciiam.createMeshPrimitive(name, options) and pass the result to setMesh().
Application geometry animation.setMesh({ positions: new Float32Array([ 0, 1, 0, -1, -1, 0, 1, -1, 0 ]), indices: new Uint16Array([0, 1, 2]), primitive: 'triangles' }); animation.setMode('mesh'); Positions are XYZ triples. Optional normals must be a matching Float32Array; optional colours contain one RGBA Float32 tuple per vertex. Indices may be unsigned 8-, 16-, or 32-bit arrays. Invalid lengths, non-finite positions, out-of-range indices, incomplete primitives, and configured complexity-limit violations are rejected before rendering.
glTF and GLB await animation.setModel('/models/product.glb', { onProgress({ loaded, total }) { console.log(total ? loaded / total : loaded); } }); animation.setMode('mesh'); setModel() accepts a URL, Blob, ArrayBuffer, typed-array view, or parsed glTF object. It supports glTF 2.0 JSON, GLB v2, data URIs, relative external buffers, interleaved accessors, sparse accessors, node hierarchies and transforms, vertex normals and colours, scene selection, and all core point/line/triangle primitive modes. A new load cancels the previous load. clearModel() cancels pending work and releases the retained geometry.
The web utility restricts local file selection to .glb. A browser cannot infer the relationship between a separately selected .gltf document and arbitrary sibling .bin files through a single-file picker. For split assets, host the .gltf and its buffers together and enter the .gltf URL in the utility, or call setModel() with that URL. Relative buffer URIs resolve against the model URL. S3 and other remote hosts must return CORS headers for both the .gltf and every referenced .bin file.
// app.js await animation.setModel('https://assets.example.com/models/object.gltf'); Application code that already has separately selected files can supply a resolver. resolveUri receives the URI stored in the glTF JSON and returns its matching File, byte buffer, or alternate URL.
// app.js const resources = new Map(selectedFiles.map((file) => [file.name, file])); await animation.setModel(gltfFile, { resolveUri(uri) { return resources.get(uri); } }); Custom decoders for compressed glTF extensions (such as KHR_draco_mesh_compression or EXT_meshopt_compression) can be registered via asciiam.registerGltfDecoder(name, decoderFn):
// Register a custom Draco or Meshopt extension decoder asciiam.registerGltfDecoder('KHR_draco_mesh_compression', async (extensionData, context) => { // Decode compressed buffer view into Float32Array positions/normals return decodedGeometry; }); The utility’s scale and field-of-view controls are 3D equivalents of the image controls, but they update meshTransform.scale and meshCamera.fov. The same meshTransform.rotation and signed scale controls rotate or mirror procedural primitives and imported models because both use the same normalized mesh pipeline.
Combining 3D meshes and images 3D meshes and background images can be used together in a single composition. When colorFromImage is enabled (true) and an image is loaded (via setImage() or the web utility image picker), 3D mesh geometry (procedural primitives or glTF/GLB models) automatically samples cell colors directly from the background image grid.
// app.js - Image-textured 3D mesh composition const animation = new asciiam('#hero', { mode: 'mesh', meshEnabled: true, // meshEnabled/imageEnabled default to false meshPrimitive: 'torus', colorFromImage: true }); await animation.setImage('/images/texture.jpg'); animation.start(); Required extensions are rejected with their names before scene mesh allocation. In particular, Draco and Meshopt decoders are not bundled, downloaded, or injectable. This keeps model behavior deterministic and the runtime dependency-free.
Controls and events API Default Purpose meshStyle wireframe points, wireframe, or solid cell rasterization. meshProjection perspective Perspective or orthographic projection. meshCamera internal camera Position, target, up vector, field of view, clipping planes, and orthographic scale. meshTransform identity Position [x, y, z], manual Euler orientation [rotX, rotY, rotZ] in radians, and scale [sx, sy, sz]. meshLight one directional light Direction, ambient contribution, and intensity. meshAutoRotate true Enables continuous auto-rotation using meshRotationSpeed against elapsed time. meshRotationSpeed [0.2, 0.45, 0.1] Sets 3-axis auto-rotation speed in radians per second [speedX, speedY, speedZ] for X (pitch), Y (yaw), and Z (roll). meshMaxVertices 100000 Rejects larger normalized geometry. meshMaxPrimitives 100000 Rejects larger point, line, or triangle counts. Model loading emits modelLoadStart, modelProgress, modelReady, modelError, and modelClear. Geometry changes emit meshReady and meshClear.
When extended diagnostics are enabled, the attached status output adds the current source kind, vertex count, primitive count, topology, and raster style. getStats().mesh exposes the same normalized geometry summary and getStats().modelLoaded distinguishes model input from directly supplied or procedural mesh input. These values are retained metadata; collecting them does not traverse vertex or index buffers per frame.
Asset and delivery policy Poly Haven publishes CC0 models. Khronos glTF Sample Assets provides format examples, but each model’s license must be checked individually. glTF/GLB is the supported import format; no third-party model is bundled with the package. See Attributions before adding a demonstration asset.
Run npm run benchmark:mesh after changing projection or rasterization code. The benchmark reference scene contains 960 vertices and 1,920 triangles at a 60×45 cell grid; the enforced desktop gate is 4 ms median and 8 ms p95.
Local benchmark on 2026-08-19: 1,200 iterations measured 0.245 ms median and 0.435 ms p95, with 309 cells drawn. This is the cell-raster stage only; browser glyph rasterization, GPU presentation, and physical-device thermal behavior require separate verification.
Reference Diagnostic Type Meaning getStats().mesh mesh summary Retained vertex, primitive, topology, style, and projection metadata. getStats().modelLoaded boolean Indicates that the active geometry originated from setModel(). Extended 3D line attached text Source kind, counts, topology, and raster style; updated at the statistics interval.
