description: Release history and behavior changes for asciiam.
text:
Unreleased Behavior change: meshEnabled/imageEnabled now default to false (chartEnabled already did) — setImage()/setMesh()/setModel() load a source but no longer show it until the corresponding flag is set explicitly. Fixed two built-in presets (imageReveal, telemetryChart) that never set their own flag and so never actually rendered anything. setLayers() layers can now carry their own independent image/imageOptions and meshPrimitive/model/modelOptions, decoded and rasterized separately from the shared instance-wide image/mesh and from every other layer’s, so different layers can show different sources at once. A layer without its own source still falls back to the shared one. Added autoQuality (default false): steps resolutionScale, then quality, down under sustained frame-time pressure and back up under headroom, never past what was requested at construction. New autoQualityChange event. Behavior change: sequence transition.type: 'morph' is now a real per-cell transition — individual ASCII cells transition character, color, and opacity (or position, in style: 'flow') instead of crossfading the whole canvas. The original whole-canvas crossfade moved to transition.type: 'blend'; an existing sequence using type: 'morph' will start getting the new per-cell behavior automatically. morph accepts style: 'dissolve' | 'scramble' | 'flow' (default 'dissolve') and spread (wavefront band width, default 0.22), and falls back to blend automatically for a setLayers() composite, a step whose own options resize the grid mid-transition, or while a step’s image/model source is still loading. See Animation sequences. Added assemble and breakApart seeded fragment modes for directional entry and exit transitions. The modes use the existing logical grid and reveal-duration controls across Canvas 2D, WebGL2, image-backed output, and headless rendering. Fixed: with the default renderer: 'auto', falling back from WebGPU to WebGL2 could leave the canvas permanently frozen on its first frame (reading as a blank/background-colored surface) because the visibility observer wasn’t re-attached to the replacement canvas element. Affected any instance that fell back off WebGPU, most visibly the docs site’s page headers and the gallery’s orbitalFlow/risingEmbers presets. Fixed (docs site build): the docs site’s own script tags and module imports (docs.js, gallery.js, examples.js, home.js, and their references to the core library bundle) were never cache-busted, unlike the Web Utility playground — a cached copy of any of them could keep serving a fixed bug after a new deploy. All now carry the same content-derived revision query string as the playground. Fixed (WebGPU): the trail overlay and backdrop surfaces shared one GPU uniform buffer with the glyph draw pass; because WebGPU only executes a frame’s draws after queue.submit(), every draw ended up reading whichever one’s data was written last (always the glyph pass’s own unrelated placeholder color), rendering trail and backdrop as solid opaque white instead of their configured color on every frame with any WebGPU adapter in use. Each draw now gets its own uniform buffer. Fixed: the imageReveal built-in preset had no image source at all, so it could never actually preview in the gallery even with imageEnabled: true. Now points at a real bundled default image. Docs-site build tooling: media assets moved from one flat, mixed-format folder into docs/assets/{images/{png,webp,svg,gifs,jpg},meshes}/, organized by type. Adding or replacing a file there is now the only step needed — the Web Utility image picker, the docs splash background, and the gallery all pick it up automatically on the next build. Not a library API change. Fixed: an empty charSet (constructor, setOption(), or a layer’s options.charSet) rendered the literal text "undefined" across the canvas instead of nothing. Fixed: an explicitly-undefined imageBrightness/imageContrast silently corrupted every sampled image pixel’s color. Fixed: _resampleImage() threw uncaught on a tainted (cross-origin, no CORS headers) image source instead of degrading gracefully. Fixed (WebGPU): gradientViews grew without bound for the life of an instance using any gradient, worst-case an animated one (gradient.animate: true) whose cache key changes roughly every 50ms forever; the underlying GPU texture cache was already correctly capped, but this parallel cache wasn’t trimmed alongside it. Bind-group caching was also being defeated on effectively every frame for an animated gradient specifically. Both fixed. Calling start() after destroy() is now a no-op instead of silently resuming the render loop against torn-down state. Web Utility playground: every slider, dropdown, and toggle now has an in-context Lume tooltip — a quick tip on the label, and for controls with real nuance, a small “i” badge with a richer, structured explanation. Not a library API change. 0.11.0 Runtime & API Extensions Multi-Layer Compositing: Introduced setLayers(), getLayers(), and options.layers for multi-pass animation blending, opacity masking, and per-layer mode composition. 3D Software Renderer Acceleration: Precomputed $4\times4$ view-model transformations for 3D GLB/glTF rendering; added registerGltfDecoder() for custom 3D model decoders. Dynamic Density & State Preservation: Integrated particle state preservation across dynamic density updates (setOption('density', ...)), retaining trajectory states for Matrix, Sparkle, Fire, Snow, Starfield, and Orbit modes during live resizing. Subpixel Font Calibration: Added calibrateFontMetrics() for subpixel character ratio measurement and high-precision ASCII canvas alignment. Headless Generator: Added renderToString() and renderFrame() for generating static ASCII strings and frame arrays in Node.js, CLI, and headless environments. Data Chart Mode: Added chart animation mode supporting 6 visualization types (bar, horizontalBar, line, sparkline, heatmap, donut), with custom titles and CSV data inputs. Sweep Timing & Delay Curves: Added sweepDuration (seconds) and delayCurve (linear, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut, stagger) options for reveal animations. Web Utility & Documentation Light Theme Support: Added comprehensive Light Theme styling across the documentation site and Web Utility with zero FOUC, theme persistence (asciiam:theme), and automatic logo color switching. Web Utility Expansion: Integrated chart mode with full interactive controls, sweep timing/delay curve selectors, and multi-layer compositing options into the Web Utility. Navigation Alignment: Restructured documentation sidebar navigation to place “Web Utility” as a primary top-level item preceding the JSON Builder. Homepage Showcase: Enhanced splash page 3D mesh resolution and added an 8-card live animation showcase grid featuring real-time procedural, media, and 3D demos. 0.10.0 Current documented baseline. This release establishes the public renderer, animation, sequencing, image-sampling, and web-utility contracts reflected in the API reference.
Runtime WebGL2 renderer with instanced glyph batching, shader gradients, trail and backdrop blending, and Canvas 2D fallback. Runtime renderer selection through auto, webgl2, and canvas2d. Ordered animation sequences with delays, durations, independent per-step mode repeat, whole-sequence looping, interruption, callbacks, and lifecycle events. Replaying a completed sequence restarts from step zero. Sequence nodes can retain, clear, or asynchronously replace image sources. Node timing waits for decoding; failures pause playback and emit sequenceStepError. Sequence nodes can also retain, clear, or asynchronously replace glTF/GLB model sources. Retained-frame morphs capture outgoing output before source preparation and reveal the live destination only after readiness. Dense, spatial, reveal, sparse-particle, image, and custom animation modes. Added irisIn, irisOut, dissolveIn, dissolveOut, lumaFold, riftLace, and echoBloom, with the global mode inventory available to image-backed output. Added hoverZone and clickZone for pointer-local and triggered interaction fields, with programmatic setCursor() and triggerInteraction() control. Expanded spatial alignment to a nine-position grid for every mode with a meaningful configurable origin. Added compact technical, geometric, circuit, wave, terminal, and minimal character sets while retaining asciiExtended as the documented default. Backdrops accept explicit behind or over placement. Exact opacity 1 in the over layer fully covers the glyph animation. Image-to-ASCII sampling with mask modes, inclusive RGB animation ranges, and independent centered horizontal and vertical output scaling. Image fitting now uses rendered glyph-cell dimensions instead of treating ASCII cells as square, preserving source proportions. Animated GIF sources capture every composited frame into an ASCII grid through WebCodecs ImageDecoder, preserve per-frame timing, and release decoded bitmaps immediately. Browser-timed sampling remains the fallback; imageFrameRate controls only that compatibility path. GIF capture keeps decode-time grids private and publishes the completed frame set at frame zero, preventing visible decode fast-forward. imageLuminance adds auto, normal, and invert mappings. Auto mode detects dark artwork on transparency so common black silhouette SVGs map to visible glyphs. Image sampling reuses its readback canvas and retains glyph atlases while animated frames change. Shared frame scheduling, visibility pausing, quality tiers, glyph atlases, and static-wave caching. Added bounded resolutionScale control for logical grid detail independent of canvas DPR, including live cell dimensions in the Web Utility. Web Utility runtime assets now share a content-derived cache revision, preventing new controls from loading with stale JavaScript. Cache-sensitive controls consistently use setOption() invalidation, and a built-site Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit suite covers pointer, renderer, canvas-output, 3D, responsive, reset, and asset-integrity behavior. Web utility Interactive web utility with preset editing, undo and redo, generated code, renderer selection, local image upload, animated-image controls, independent image-axis controls, and luminance mapping. 3D primitives and glTF/GLB upload use a dedicated toolbar control immediately after Image. Local 3D upload is limited to self-contained GLB. The 3D menu can load remote glTF/GLB URLs, including relative external .bin buffers, and exposes geometry scale, camera FOV, and rotation controls. Added resolveUri for application-managed glTF plus external-buffer input, image rotation and mirroring, and shared rotation/mirroring controls for procedural and imported meshes. Sequence steps expose a mode-repeat switch enabled by default for utility previews; exported configuration retains the explicit value. Replaced the vertical sequence stack with an ordered node flow and per-node image-source controls. Split web-utility behavior into a module entry point plus focused code-formatting and sequence-data modules; documentation scripts remain separated by site-wide and page-specific responsibility. Kept Reset in the primary dock and aligned Documentation, About, and FPS as direct stage actions. Kept quality, charset, alignment, and backdrop in the primary toolbar; workspace actions remain under Advanced. Character-set selection includes the expanded built-in inventory; interaction modes expose radius and duration controls; spatial alignment exposes all nine anchors. Versioned runtime loading and revalidated local library caching prevent new controls from executing against an older renderer bundle. Image-library cards use generated static 320×180 WebP previews, first-frame GIF thumbnails, low-priority lazy decoding, and off-screen content containment. Opening the Image popover no longer decodes every original media asset. Documentation Audited the README and authored documentation for direct language and factual alignment with the released package and runtime. Hugo documentation source and a live preset gallery limited to six concurrent renderers. Constructor, option, method, renderer, sequence, event, and callback reference. Web-utility workflow, preset gallery, version policy, GIF/SVG behavior, and integration guides. Default and included character sets are documented in a focused guide and the repository README. Added a single-instance usage editor with examples from minimum initialization through a broad serializable configuration, reset and copy controls, and web-utility configuration transfer. Added page descriptions, dates, tags, keywords, modified-time metadata, and GitLab/GitHub edit links across the documentation set. Added / alongside Ctrl+K and Command+K for current-page search focus. Hardened site search with combobox semantics, deduplicated index loading, stale-query suppression, malformed-field tolerance, and deploy-path-safe result links. Expanded search metadata and vocabulary aliases, added safe literal-word highlighting, and visually selected matching tag chips. Made the documentation root a chrome-free splash with an asciiam-rendered background; inner documentation pages retain navigation and search. Corrected the splash height to 100svh on desktop and mobile so its canvas owns the complete initial viewport and documentation content begins below the fold. Added maintained Lucide, SVG Repo, PAT, media-provider, registry, and delivery-service attribution references. Compatibility Canonical .mjs ESM and .cjs CommonJS package entries are provided alongside the readable/minified browser ESM and UMD bundles. Canvas 2D and requestAnimationFrame are required. WebGL2, IntersectionObserver, and ResizeObserver are feature-detected. Upgrade notes This is the first documented API baseline; there are no earlier documented migrations. Prefer renderer: 'auto' when the application should use WebGL2 where available and retain Canvas 2D fallback. Call destroy() when removing an instance so observers, listeners, renderer resources, and scheduler membership are released. Pass { animated: true } to setImage() for uploaded GIF blob URLs because their URL strings contain neither a .gif suffix nor an image/gif data-URL prefix. Use imageLuminance: 'normal' when automatic silhouette detection is not appropriate for a transparent source.
title: Changelog

description: Configure, validate, export, and persist asciiam settings in the browser utility.
text:
The web utility is an authoring surface for asciiam option objects; detailed runtime behavior remains defined by the package API.
Composition authoring & usage examples The web utility and the Usage examples playground form a unified composition authoring environment. Start with a preset, an animation mode, or a serializable example from the playground, then adjust renderer, quality, character density, spatial origin, motion, color, backdrop, images, and 3D meshes.
Reset restores default utility settings (including clearing loaded images and 3D meshes to return to the default procedural composition) while preserving named local presets. Undo and Redo operate across the browser session.
Combined 3D mesh & image compositions 3D meshes and background images can be combined into hybrid compositions. When an image is loaded and Color from image (colorFromImage) is enabled, active 3D meshes (primitives or imported glTF/GLB models) sample their cell colors directly from the background image grid.
The Character set control includes the documented asciiExtended default, ordered density ramps, symbolic palettes, and a custom string editor. Hover Zone and Click Zone expose radius and click-duration controls in Motion. Align provides nine spatial anchors.
The dock keeps Preset, Quality, Sequence, Mode, Character set, Motion, Align, Color, Backdrop, Reset, Image, 3D, and Code directly available. Advanced contains theme and history controls. Reset intentionally remains outside Advanced. Documentation, About, and the FPS switch form one level action row on the stage.
Quality includes a 0–540 FPS cap (0 for Auto/uncapped VSync, default 60 FPS) and a Grid resolution slider. 100% retains automatic grid measurement; 50% reduces cell count for constrained devices, while values up to 200% increase logical detail. The live status reports the resulting columns and rows. This setting changes glyph-grid resolution, not canvas DPR.
The sequence editor is a horizontally ordered node flow. Each node edits its animation, image-source action, duration, stagger, repeat policy, transition, and JSON option overrides. Nodes can retain or clear the current image, or load an included image; reordering changes playback order immediately.
Preview presentation types Background, Hero card, and Splash page are presentation previews rather than HTML overlays generated by asciiam. Each preview gives the renderer a bounded target and places ordinary interface content beside or above it.
Hero and Splash can use an uploaded or included image as the ASCII source. The image is sampled into glyph density and optional sampled color; the original bitmap is not placed over the preview. Use cover or contain, image scale, field of view, the global animation mode, and an optional inclusive RGB animation range to control the result.
Preview Purpose Runtime implication Background Evaluate a full-stage ASCII surface behind application content. One target sized to the stage. Hero card Evaluate ASCII image or procedural media inside a bounded content card. One renderer attached to the card media region. Splash page Evaluate a larger introductory composition and transition sequence. One renderer attached to the splash media region. Validate performance Choose auto to request WebGPU first when supported, then WebGL2, with Canvas 2D fallback. Enable FPS for the existing compact frame-rate, grid, and drawn-cell line. Enable Extended diagnostics in Quality for estimated display cadence, CPU-side frame work, fill-history text charts, renderer details, and active 3D geometry counts. The extended path is off by default and automatically enables FPS because it owns no independent update loop. Test the composition at the actual target size because density, DPR, glyph count, and image sampling work change with dimensions.
For grids and galleries, construct only visible previews and destroy instances that leave the working set. All running instances share a frame scheduler, but each WebGL2 context and glyph buffer still consumes browser resources.
Export and integrate Open Code to generate a constructor option object from the current controls. Create the instance after its target has measurable dimensions, then call start().
app.js
import asciiam from '@staticcanvas/asciiam'; const animation = new asciiam('#hero-media', { ...asciiam.presets.heroWave, renderer: 'auto' }); animation.start(); Call destroy() when removing the target. This releases observers, subscriptions, presentation resources, and an owned canvas.
The Usage examples editor provides a second configuration path. Its View in web utility action sends options representable as JSON through a base64url-encoded config query value. The utility applies that configuration after defaults and locally restored settings, then labels it as a custom configuration. Invalid or non-object values are ignored.
Persistence and local data Data Persistence Utility options Stored in versioned browser local storage. Named presets Stored locally in the current browser. Undo and redo history Retained for the current page session. Uploaded images Browser-local object URLs; not restored on the next visit. Included image/mesh manifest Generated from docs/assets/images/* and docs/assets/meshes by npm run prepare:bg. Generated code Derived from current state and not stored separately. Documentation routes Use Start for source setup and browser initialization. Use Renderers and performance for backend and quality behavior. Use Images and colour-range animation for sampled media. Use Animation sequences for staggered and interruptible flows. Use Usage examples for editable configurations. Use the API reference for option and method contracts. Reference Utility control Runtime option or API Default behavior Renderer renderer, setRenderer() auto; WebGPU first, WebGL2, then Canvas 2D fallback. Quality quality, resolutionScale, maxDPR, targetFPS Uses the selected quality tier, a 0–540 FPS cap (default 60 FPS, 0 for Auto), and 100% logical resolution. Extended diagnostics showStats, extendedStats, getStats() Disabled; samples only when explicitly enabled. Mode mode, setMode() Selects the active cell algorithm. Motion and Align speed, edgeFade, trail, pulse, align Updates animation and spatial state. Color and Backdrop color, gradient, backdrop Configures glyph and independent backdrop presentation. Image setImage(), image options Samples a local or remote image into the glyph grid. 3D setModel(), meshTransform, meshCamera, rotation options Uploads local GLB, loads remote glTF/GLB, and controls geometry scale, FOV, and rotation. Sequence setSequence(), sequence methods Configures ordered animation steps. Code constructor options Serializes the current supported configuration. config URL value JSON-representable constructor options Imports a documentation example without depending on npm or a CDN. Backdrop placement is explicit. behind draws before glyphs. over composites after glyphs, so opacity 1 fully covers the animation. The range and exact numeric input both accept the inclusive interval from 0 through 1.
The Image popover exposes centered uniform, horizontal, and vertical scaling; field of view; silhouette-aware luminance mapping; animated-image playback and sample rate; sampled color; and an optional RGB animation range. The global Mode popover remains the animation selector after an image is loaded.
The 3D popover accepts local .glb files. Its remote URL field accepts .gltf or .glb; relative .bin references are resolved from a remote .gltf URL and require CORS access. Uniform and axis scale, camera FOV, auto-rotation, and Y rotation speed are exported in generated configuration. Rotation and flip controls follow the same ownership rule: image controls transform the sampled source, while the 3D controls transform both procedural primitives and imported models through meshTransform.
npm run prepare:bg generates static 320×180 WebP menu previews when ImageMagick is available. GIF previews use the first frame and image orientation is normalized during generation. Opening the Image popover therefore decodes bounded static previews, not full-resolution sources or animated GIF streams. An original asset is loaded only after its card is selected.

description: Source, license, and service references for icons, demonstration media, mesh research, registries, and delivery infrastructure.
text:
This page identifies third-party material and external services referenced by the repository; it does not change the MIT license applied to asciiam source code.
Embedded icon paths The documentation navigation embeds a local subset of Lucide SVG paths. Lucide is distributed under the ISC License, and some Lucide designs derive from Feather under the MIT License. The redistributed notices are preserved in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Icons are embedded locally so documentation navigation does not depend on a client-side icon package or third-party request.
Bundled SVG demonstration asset docs/static/webutil/assets/images/bird-silhouette.svg is the Bird Shape vector from SVG Repo. SVG Repo identifies that asset as CC0. The file remains a demonstration input for silhouette-aware image-to-ASCII conversion.
Map reference docs/static/webutil/assets/images/earth-landmask-256-slow.gif uses a globe land-mask source associated with PAT, the free, open-source portable atlas. PAT states that its maps and generating scripts are public domain.
Demonstration photographs The image library contains demonstration and rendering-test media sourced from Pexels, Pixabay, and local repository contributions. Provider and creator identifiers are retained in filenames where available. Provider references are not blanket license claims: verify an individual source record before redistributing an asset outside this repository.
3D model sources and format references The documentation bundles Poly Haven’s Classic Laptop GLB as the live 3D canvas on the splash page. The model is by Arrangemonk, contains 14,450 triangles, and is distributed under Poly Haven’s CC0 asset license. The staged 2K GLB is classic-laptop-2k.glb; materials and textures are not rendered by asciiam’s bounded mesh pipeline.
The dependency-free glTF/GLB loader also uses the following format and candidate sources:
